{{nihongo|'''Kojino Shrine'''|己爾乃神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

[[ja:己爾乃神社]]

The Kujo-family annotated text reads "Kojino" as "Konino."</ref>.

Before land reclamation, the south branch of the {{ill|Yasu River|ceb|Yasu-gawa|fa|رود یاسو|fr|Yasu-gawa|ja|野洲川|ru|Ясу (река)|qid=Q8049935}} flowing from the Yasu River to {{ill|Lake Biwa|ar|بحيرة بيوا|arz|بحيره بيوا|az|Biva gölü|ban|Danu Biwa|bat_smg|Bivas ežers|bcl|Danaw nin Biwa|be|Біва|be_x_old|Біва|bg|Бива (езеро)|bs|Biwa (jezero)|ca|Llac Biwa|ceb|Biwa-ko|cs|Biwa|cv|Бива (кӳлĕ)|de|Biwa-See|el|Λίμνη Μπίβα|eo|Lago Biŭa|es|Lago Biwa|et|Biwa järv|eu|Biwa aintzira|fa|دریاچه بیوا|fi|Biwa (järvi)|fr|Lac Biwa|he|אגם ביווה|hi|बिवा झील|hr|Biwa|hu|Biva-tó|hy|Բիվա լիճ|id|Danau Biwa|it|Lago Biwa|ja|琵琶湖|ka|ბივა|ko|비와호|la|Lacus Biwa|lt|Biva (ežeras)|lv|Bivas ezers|ml|ബിവ തടാകം|mn|Бива нуур|my|ဘိဝရေကန်|nl|Biwameer|no|Biwasjøen|pl|Biwa (jezioro)|pt|Lago Biwa|qu|Biwa qucha|ro|Lacul Biwa|ru|Бива (озеро)|simple|Lake Biwa|sl|Biva|sr|Бива (језеро)|sv|Biwasjön|sw|Ziwa Biwa|th|ทะเลสาบบิวะ|tr|Biwa Gölü|uk|Біва (озеро)|uz|Biva|vi|Hồ Biwa|zh|琵琶湖|zh_min_nan|Pî-pê-ô͘|zh_yue|琵琶湖|qid=Q200239}} ran between them, and both stood on the left-bank levee, so they are thought to originate in river-related worship<ref name="調査報告">''Shikinaisha Chosa Hokoku''.</ref>. Both preserve traditions of being the Shikinaisha, but it is geographically and historically impossible to determine one as the sole original shrine; rather, it has been pointed out that the Engishiki "Kojino Shrine" may have consisted of both shrines, which may once have had close ritual ties<ref name="調査報告"/>.

It is located in Kaihatsu, Sumoto-cho. From its location it is called "Kaihatsu no Kojino Shrine," but because a bridge called "Retsukeizu-bashi" once crossed the former south branch of the Yasu River nearby before reclamation, it was also called "Retsukeizu no Kojino Shrine"<ref name="調査報告"/>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
It enshrines {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}} as principal deities, with {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ikatsuchi no Omi no Mikoto}} as associated deities.

Formerly the two associated deities were the principal deities under the names '''{{ill|Nyakuichi Ōji|Q11616186|qid=Q11616186}}''' (for Ame-no-Koyane) and '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakaichi Gongen}}''' (for Ikatsuchi-no-Omi), but on September 22, {{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}} (Meiji 14), they were changed to the current arrangement<ref name="調査報告"/>.

=== Origin ===
Shrine tradition says it was founded in {{ill|829|Q30357|qid=Q30357}} ({{ill|Tenchō|de|Tenchō|es|Tenchō|fa|تنچو|fr|Ère Tenchō|ia|Tencho|id|Tenchō|ja|天長|ko|덴초|ru|Тэнтё|simple|Tenchō|sr|Тенчо|th|เท็นโจ|tr|Tenchō|uk|Тентьо|zh|天長 (日本)|zh_yue|天長 (年號)|qid=Q1373138}} 6) by Iga Atsumu. Atsumu, also called "Taifu Atsumu," is said to be a descendant of the Iga clan, whose ancestor was Iga no Suketoyo. Since the Iga clan was related to the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|Q1198447|qid=Q1198447}}<ref>''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362}}'', Sakyo Shinbetsu-jō.</ref>, it is said they enshrined Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto and Ikatsuchi-no-Omi-no-Mikoto, ancestral deities of the Nakatomi clan<ref name="神社庁開発">Shiga Prefecture Shrine Office, "[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=463 Kojino Shrine]" (accessed Feb. 28, 2010).</ref>. Because it was often damaged by flooding of the Yasu River, only one volume titled ''Kojino Jinja no Engi-gaki'' remains, while treasures and old records were lost<ref name="調査報告"/>. There was also a shrine temple called {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakaichioji Temple}}, and present-day {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Renko-ji}} is said to continue its line. ''{{ill|Omi Yochi Shiryaku|Q85883966|qid=Q85883966}}'' records a {{ill|Bhaiṣajyaguru Hall|Q11622438|qid=Q11622438}} near the shrine with a Buddhist image said to be made by Dengyo Daishi ({{ill|Saichō|az|Sayço|cs|Saičó|de|Saichō|es|Saichō|et|Saichō|eu|Saichō|fa|سایچو|fr|Saichō|id|Saichō|it|Saichō|ja|最澄|ko|사이초|nl|Saicho|no|Saichō|pl|Saichō|pt|Saicho|ro|Saichō|ru|Сайтё|sh|Saichō|sl|Saičo|sr|Саићо|sv|Saichō|tr|Saichō|uk|Сайтьо|vi|Tối Trừng|zh|最澄|qid=Q449943}}), and this is inferred to have housed the shrine's {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=honji-butsu}}<ref name="調査報告"/>. Later it received a Senior First Rank {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sogen Senji}} from the {{ill|Yoshida family|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722}} of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jingi Kanryo}}, and still preserves a sacred mirror inscribed "Senior First Rank Wakaichi Daigongen"<ref name="神社庁開発"/>. Its former rank was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

Located in Nakanomae, Sumoto-cho. From its location it is called "Nakanomae no Kojino Shrine" and "Ōmagari no Kojino Shrine" (Ōmagari was the old local area name adjacent to Nakanomae)<ref name="調査報告"/>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
It enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōanamuji-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Amatsuhikone|Q10940228|qid=Q10940228|lt=Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}.

=== Origin ===
Tradition says it was founded by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakatomi Tamee}} in {{ill|703|Q23500|qid=Q23500}} ({{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 3). Though shrine buildings were lost in warfare during the {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} era (1558-1570), they were restored by {{ill|1791|Q7784|qid=Q7784}} ({{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 3). Nearby {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gyokurin-ji}} was formerly its shrine temple<ref name="調査報告"/>. Its former rank was village shrine.

A {{ill|Copper|Q753|qid=Q753}} {{ill|kyōzutsu|Q11606503|qid=Q11606503}} from the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}. Designated as Moriyama City cultural property (craft) on August 26, {{ill|1974|Q2478|qid=Q2478}} (Showa 49).
